ranking.note: Raised to P2 and moved up: same class of defect as P1 #35837 (RPC reports missing data instead of surfacing an internal failure), so it cannot sit among ordinary feature work.
Moved up: file-clobbering on concurrent dumptxoutset runs is a data-corruption edge case, ahead of purely additive RPC features.
Moved up: a silently disabled configured ZMQ interface is an operator-visible reliability bug, ranked with the other interface bug fixes.
Moved up: mining clients receiving 'Internal bug detected' on shutdown is a real caller-facing defect, grouped with the other bug fixes rather than after features.
Moved up to sit with the other small caller-facing output bugs; hidden warnings are a correctness-of-returned-data issue.
Moved up: two RPCs returning contradictory progress values is an inconsistency of returned data, which this category weights above new methods.
Moved down slightly: a valuable API gap, but bug fixes to existing behavior precede a new pre-flight method.
Moved up: removes a long-standing capability restriction for pruned operators, a larger benefit than the other additive RPC fields.
Moved down: issue-backed REST parity gap, but ranked behind existing-behavior fixes per category ordering.
Moved down: additive output fields rank behind correctness fixes to data already returned.
Moved down: new observability RPC with a feature request behind it, but no downstream consumer blocked, so it sits with the other additive methods.
Moved down: opt-in management RPCs with no external consumer asking, ranked with other additive features.
Raised to P3: it is the competing alternative to #34038 for the same trace-logging problem and must share that PR's band.
Moved down: test-only RPC convenience with no external consumer, ranked with the lowest-value additive changes.
Moved down: an unrequested diagnostic field; per this category new fields without an asking consumer rank near the bottom of P3.
Lowered to P4: self-described internal refactor with no bug fix or behavior change, weaker than the P3 HTTP work it follows.
Lowered to P4: micro-optimization whose benchmark scenario (10k unbroadcast IDs) does not occur in practice.

inconsistencies: Three PRs compete on the same trace-logging problem: #34038 (ajtowns, -trace + logging RPC schema change), #35387 (ryanofsky, -loglevel + new loglevel RPC), and #35355 (ajtowns, atomics draft that also carries the #34038 deprecations). Reviewers should first decide between #34038 and #35387 — they are mutually exclusive interface designs — before spending time on #35355's overlapping half.

#36351 (dumptxoutset rollback crash on pruned node) and #36266 (dumptxoutset early-fail on stale targets / concurrent runs) touch the same RPC's pre-flight checks and will likely conflict. Review #36351 first: it fixes a daemon abort, and #36266's stale-target check can be rebased on top.

#35837 (scanblocks silently returning completed:true over an unindexed range) and #35728 (GetTransaction reporting confirmed transactions as missing on I/O errors) are the same failure discipline — RPCs reporting success/absence instead of an error. Settling the error-code convention in #35837 should guide #35728.

Large HTTP-server cluster from the post-libevent rewrite will conflict: #36187, #36200, #36204, #36259, #35780, #36303, #36159, #36124. Suggested order: #36187 (bind/security) → #36200 and #36204 (resource exhaustion) → #36259 and #35780 (response-delivery races, both touch close/send paths) → #36303/#36159 (tests, logging) → #36124 (encapsulation refactor, which by its own description follows up review of the already-merged #35829).

#33904 and #35909 both extend the REST interface toward RPC parity under the same tracking issue (#33808 / #35897); they are independent but should be reviewed with one consistent decision on how far REST parity is wanted, and #35909's shared boolean-query-parameter helper may be reused by #33904.

#36300 is a release-branch backport of already-merged master PRs; its rpc-relevant content (#36297 OpenRPC metadata defaults) duplicates work already reviewed on master, so it needs release-branch verification only, not fresh design review.
result.notes: The category is dominated by the newly rewritten internal HTTP server: the two P1s and most of the P2s are interface security, DoS, and response-delivery defects introduced or exposed there, and they should absorb review attention before the long tail of additive RPC fields and methods. Applying the category's own rule that new methods without an asking consumer rank low pushed several feature PRs (#31672, #32468, #34534, #29418) toward the bottom of P3 without changing their bands.
